native_result.query: In what context does the gardening pathway for introducing non-native plants show different prevalence styles across habitat types?
native_result.HypoA: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats.
native_result.HypoB: The gardening pathway for introducing non-native plants shows different prevalence styles across habitat types: it is proportionally dominant in natural/semi-natural and coastal-wetland habitats — in forests gardening species constitute nearly the entire alien flora (100% in broad-leaved, 88% in coniferous; low-evidence) and in wetlands and coastal habitats it is the leading pathway (~55% of alien records, present in ~45-50% of plots; both significantly more gardening-dominated than other high-evidence habitats, p=6.3e-04 and 6.7e-03) — whereas in the most human-modified, alien-rich habitats (urban, croplands) gardening is a minority share (29% and 19%) despite being frequently present (~48% of urban plots), because unintentional introductions dominate there (69-77% of records; croplands significantly gardening-poor, p=2.2e-04). Habitat x pathway composition differs highly significantly (pooled chi-square 66.20, df=12, p=1.6e-09; permutation p=5e-05). This pattern aligns with the regional temporal trend in which gardening became the dominant introduction pathway over time (share of first records 17% before 1500 to 75% in 1985-2019), suggesting gardening prevails as the introducer of aliens in natural/coastal-wetland contexts while unintentional introductions prevail in urban and agricultural contexts.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded invaded_niche_pathways.csv (632 plots, 37 cols, tab-delimited); verified n.gard+n.unint+n.agfo==n.total in all rows (integer counts). Built habitat x pathway contingency table (10 habitats x 3 pathways). Computed per-habitat prevalence styles: gardening share of alien records, per-plot mean gardening count (all plots as denominator incl. n.total=0), per-plot gardening presence frequency, and dominant pathway. Tested composition differences with chi-square after pooling habitats with <10 alien records (Coniferous, Broad-leaved, Scrublands, Rock outcrops), cross-checked with a 20,000-permutation exact test on fixed margins; pairwise 2xK chi-squares for high-evidence habitats. Used invasion_success_pathways.csv (81 species; Gardening 42, Unintentional 30, AgriForest 9) and temporal_trends_contingency_table.csv (regional first records) as context only, not merged; phylogenetic_tree.txt linkage confirmed (76/81 tips) but not required for this question. Caveats documented: counting semantics (species vs occurrences, possible multi-pathway assignment) undocumented; zero-alien plots assumed true absences; small-cell habitats marked low-evidence and excluded from the primary claim.

sub_hypo.text: Gardening is the leading introduction pathway in wetlands and coastal habitats, representing approximately 55% of alien records and occurring in approximately 45–50% of plots; these habitats are significantly more gardening-dominated than other high-evidence habitats.
sub_hypo.context: Wetland and coastal habitat plots in Barcelona province, compared with other high-evidence habitats.
sub_hypo.relations: Gardening has the largest pathway share, approximately 55% of alien records; n.gard > 0 in approximately 45–50% of plots. Gardening dominance differs significantly from other high-evidence habitats, with p=6.3e-04 for wetlands and p=6.7e-03 for coastal habitats.

sub_hypo.text: In human-modified, alien-rich urban habitats and croplands, gardening contributes a minority of alien records despite frequent presence in urban plots, while unintentional introductions dominate.
sub_hypo.context: Urban and cropland plots in Barcelona province; presence frequencies include all plots, treating zero-alien plots as true absences.
sub_hypo.relations: Gardening accounts for 29% of urban alien records and 19% of cropland alien records, while occurring in approximately 48% of urban plots. Unintentional introductions account for 69–77% of records in these habitats. Croplands are significantly gardening-poor relative to other high-evidence habitats (p=2.2e-04).

sub_hypo.text: The composition of non-native plant introduction pathways differs highly significantly among habitat types.
sub_hypo.context: 632 plots across 10 habitat types in Barcelona province. Coniferous forests, broad-leaved forests, scrublands, and rock outcrops, each with fewer than 10 alien records, were pooled for the overall test; count semantics and possible multi-pathway assignment are undocumented.

sub_hypo.text: Gardening became the dominant regional introduction pathway over time, with its share of first records increasing from 17% before 1500 to 75% in 1985–2019.
sub_hypo.context: Regional first records of non-native flora in Catalonia; temporal data provide context only and were not merged with the Barcelona habitat data.
sub_hypo.relations: Gardening's proportion of first-record counts increases across introduction periods, from 17% before 1500 to 75% in 1985–2019. This contextual trend aligns with gardening dominance in natural/coastal-wetland habitats, without establishing a directly tested temporal–habitat relationship.
